 nomination at the 28th Screen Actors Guild Awards for Outstanding
 Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture . [ 238 ] On February 24, 2023, following months-long renewed interest in and virality of the
 Weeknd's 2016 song "Die for You", a remix of the song with Grande was
 released. It marked their fourth collaboration. [ 239 ] The remix topped the Billboard Hot 100 chart, becoming both artists' seventh number-one hit.
 Grande became the artist with the most number-one duets (four) on the chart,
 surpassing McCartney. [ 240 ] According to the International
 Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), it was the fourth best-selling song of 2023 globally. [ 241 ] On August 25, 2023, Grande
 released a reissue of her debut studio album, Yours Truly (Tenth Anniversary
 Edition) . [ 242 ] [ 243 ] On December 9, 2023, Grande
 and Jennifer Hudson made a surprise appearance onstage to sing the "Oh Santa!" remix
 at Mariah Carey's show at the Madison Square Garden , of her Merry Christmas One and All! tour. [ 244 ]

sections.heading: 2024–present: Eternal Sunshine , Wicked , and focus on acting
sections.text:
Grande's seventh studio album, titled Eternal Sunshine , was released on
 March 8, 2024. It was preceded by its lead single, " Yes, And? ", released on January 12. [ 245 ] The song debuted at number
 one on the Billboard Hot 100, [ 246 ] topped the Billboard Global 200 and Global Excl. US charts for two weeks, [ 247 ] and was followed by a remix
 featuring Mariah Carey on
 February 16. [ 248 ] The second single, " We Can't Be Friends (Wait
 for Your Love) ", was released in tandem with the album. [ 249 ] Grande's first album in over
 three years, [ 250 ] Eternal Sunshine marked her first major foray into dance and house music. [ 251 ] [ 252 ] Met with universal acclaim,
 critics dubbed it one of her most mature and sophisticated records yet. [ 253 ] Both the album and its
 second single debuted atop the Billboard 200 and the Hot 100
 respectively, [ 254 ] achieving Grande's
 third-largest sales week (227,000 units) and making her the woman with the most Hot 100
 number-one debuts (7). [ 255 ] [ 256 ] Elsewhere, the album debuted
 at number one in thirteen countries, including Australia, [ 257 ] Canada, [ 258 ] and the UK. [ 259 ] With Eternal Sunshine and Thank U, Next , Grande became the first woman to have two albums produce
 multiple number-one single debuts in the US. [ 254 ] It also marked her first
 instance of reaching the top of both the Billboard Hot 100
 Songwriters and Hot 100 Producers charts. [ 260 ] Topping the Pop Airplay chart for two
 weeks, [ 261 ] "We Can't Be Friends (Wait
 for Your Love)" marked Grande's tenth number-one. [ 262 ] On May 6, 2024, Grande performed at the Met
 Gala , and was joined on stage by Cynthia Erivo to close out her performance. [ 263 ] " The Boy Is Mine ", which reached
 the top 20 on the Hot 100, [ 264 ] was issued as the third Eternal Sunshine single in June; [ 265 ] a remix featuring Brandy and Monica followed later
 that month. [ 266 ] On August 22, 2024, Grande
 released a reissue of her second studio album, My Everything , for the tenth
 anniversary of the record. [ 267 ] Two extended editions of Eternal Sunshine containing the pre-released single remixes, guest vocals
 from Troye Sivan , and live
 versions of several tracks, were surprise released in March and October 2024. [ 268 ] [ 269 ] Grande appeared as the
 musical guest on Saturday Night Live on March 9, 2024 , to promote Eternal
 Sunshine . [ 270 ] She featured on the remix to
 " Sympathy Is a Knife " on Charli XCX 's remix album Brat and
 It's Completely Different but Also Still Brat , released on October
 11, 2024. [ 271 ] On the Las Culturistas podcast, Grande acknowledged that she would likely scale back her pop music output
 compared to earlier in her career, shifting her focus more towards acting. [ 272 ] Eternal Sunshine was
 ranked as 2024's thirteenth-best-selling and ninth-most-streamed album globally by
 the International
 Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI). [ 273 ] At the 67th Annual Grammy Awards , Grande was
 nominated for Best Pop Vocal Album ( Eternal Sunshine ), Best Pop Duo/Group
 Performance ("The Boy Is Mine" remix), and Best Dance Pop Recording ("Yes, And?"). [ 274 ] Eternal Sunshine
 Deluxe: Brighter Days Ahead , a reissue of Eternal Sunshine ,
 was released on March 28, 2025. [ 275 ] Grande starred as the
 protagonist Peaches in the accompanying short film Brighter Days
 Ahead , which she directed and wrote with Christian
 Breslauer ; it was released on the same day. Her directorial debut, [ 276 ] the short film won the Video of the Year award
 at the 2025 MTV Video Music Awards . [ 277 ] With the release of the
 reissue, Eternal Sunshine became Grande's longest-running number one album in
 the US (three weeks). [ 278 ] Aided by Brighter Days
 Ahead , the album returned to the top of the charts in Australia, Canada,
 Ireland, and New Zealand, over a year after its release. [ 279 ] The bonus track " Twilight Zone " was released as
 the reissue's lead single in April 2025, reaching the top ten on the Billboard Global 200 and the UK singles chart. [ 280 ] [ 281 ] Later that month, Grande
 featured on Jeff Goldblum and the Mildred Snitzer Orchestra's jazz album Still Blooming for a rendition
 of the song " I Don't Know Why (I Just Do) ". [ 282 ] She and Mariah Carey joined Barbra Streisand on
 "One Heart, One Voice" for Streisand's album The Secret of Life:
 Partners, Volume Two , released on June 27, 2025. [ 283 ] Whilst describing the three
 as "the holy trinity of glorious sound", Melissa Ruggieri of USA Today called the track
 an "otherwise generic ballad [that] showcases a trio steeped in restraint". [ 284 ] Grande starred as Galinda Upland ,
 alongside Cynthia Erivo as Elphaba Thropp , in the two-part film adaptation of the fantasy
 musical Wicked ,
 directed by Jon M. Chu . [ 285 ] She was cast in November
 2021, and had auditioned five times for the role. [ 286 ] She was credited with her
 birth name Ariana Grande-Butera, which was her name when she first saw the stage
 musical at age 10. [ 287 ] Grande reported that she
 began taking acting and singing lessons months before she auditioned for the role of
 Glinda because she wanted to be cast "so badly". [ 288 ] The first part, Wicked ,
 was theatrically released in November 2024, [ 289 ] followed by the second part, Wicked: For
 Good , in November 2025. [ 290 ] Critically acclaimed, Wicked was regarded amongst the best musical films of the 21st century and
 declared a pop culture phenomenon by various media. [ 291 ] [ 292 ] For Good was met with
 lukewarm reviews and less enthusiasm than its predecessor. [ 293 ] The two parts grossed
 US$759 million and US$535 million worldwide, becoming the highest-grossing
 and third-highest-grossing musical adaptation films of all time, respectively. [ 294 ] Grande's performance and
 comedic timing received praise from critics; [ 295 ] she was nominated for
 supporting actress categories at the 97th Academy Awards , the 82nd and 83rd Golden Globe Awards , the 30th and 31st Critics' Choice Awards , the 31st and 32nd
 Screen Actors Guild Awards and the 78th British Academy Film
 Awards . [ 296 ] The films'
 soundtracks were co-billed to Grande, who performed several songs from the
 musical and an original track titled " The Girl in the Bubble ", written by Stephen Schwartz for
 the Wicked: For Good soundtrack . [ 297 ] Both albums received
 positive reviews and debuted at number two on the Billboard 200 with 139,000
 and 122,000 units, tying for the highest debut for a soundtrack to a stage-to-film adaptation . [ 298 ] [ 299 ] Grande and her co-star
 Erivo's rendition of " Defying Gravity " won Best Pop Duo/Group
 Performance at the 68th Annual Grammy Awards . [ 300 ] To promote the Wicked films, Grande hosted Saturday Night Live on October 12, 2024 and December 20, 2025 . [ 301 ] [ 302 ] Her 2024 episode drew the
 show's highest ratings since May 2021, at the time, and became its most-watched
 episode on Peacock and across social media; [ 303 ] the 2025 episode was that
 year and season 51 's highest-rated and SNL ' s
 most-watched holiday episode since 2020. [ 304 ] She and Erivo opened the
 97th Academy Awards ceremony with a medley of " Over the Rainbow ", " Home ", and " Defying
 Gravity ". [ 305 ] In November 2025, Grande
 appeared in the special Wicked: One Wonderful Night ,
 performing music from the Wicked films alongside the cast; [ 306 ] a live album of the special
 was released in tandem with the broadcast. [ 307 ] In 2026, she will embark on the Eternal Sunshine Tour , her first
 concert tour since 2019, with 41 shows between June and September. [ 308 ] [ 309 ] Grande's upcoming film
 projects include Focker
 In-Law (2026) [ 310 ] and an animated film
 adaptation of Dr. Seuss 's 1990 book Oh, the Places You'll Go! ,
 slated for release in March 2028. [ 311 ] She will star in the
 thirteenth season of the horror anthology series American
 Horror Story , which will start filming by spring 2026. [ 312 ] In the summer of 2027,
 Grande will make her London stage debut opposite her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in Marianne Elliott 's Barbican Theatre production of Sunday in the Park with
 George . [ 313 ] Grande's music is generally pop and R&B with
 elements of EDM , hip hop , [ 314 ] [ 315 ] and trap , [ 316 ] the latter first appearing
 prominently on her Christmas & Chill extended play.
 While consistently maintaining pop and R&B tones, she has increasingly
 incorporated trap into her music as her career has progressed, [ 317 ] thanks to her work with record producer Tommy
 Brown. [ 318 ] She has collaborated with
 Brown on every album thus far and stated that "one of the things I love most about
 working with Tommy is that none of the beats he plays me ever sound the same." [ 319 ] Grande learned how to sound
 engineer and produce her own vocals because she "love[s] being hands on"
 with every project, revealing that rapper Mac Miller first taught her how to use the digital
 audio workstation Pro
 Tools . [ 320 ] Collaborator Justin Tranter remarked
 that he felt inspired seeing how involved Grande is in creating her music "from the
 writing to the vision to the storytelling and to even engineering and comping her
 own vocals." [ 321 ] She has co-written songs
 addressing a wide variety of themes, such as love, sex, wealth, breakups,
 independence, empowerment, self-love and moving on from the past. [ 322 ] Grande's debut album Yours Truly was complimented for recreating the R&B
 "vibe and feel of the 90s" with the help of songwriter and producer Babyface . [ 323 ] Her follow-up record, My
 Everything , explored EDM and electropop genres. [ 324 ] Grande expanded the pop and
 R&B sound on her third album, Dangerous Woman , which was praised by the Los Angeles
 Times for integrating elements of different styles, such as reggae -pop ("Side to Side"), dance-pop
 ("Be Alright"), and guitar -trap fusion
 ("Sometimes"). [ 325 ] Trap-pop was more heavily
 featured on her fourth and fifth studio albums, Sweetener and Thank U,
 Next . [ 317 ] Elias Leight of Rolling Stone opined that Grande "set her sights on conquering trap, savage basslines and jittery
 swarms of drum programming" and "embrace[d] the sound of hard-bitten Southern
 hip-hop" on Sweetener , exploring funk music with themes of love and prosperity. [ 326 ] [ 327 ] Craig Jenkins of Vulture noted that she embraced trap and hip hop with undertones of R&B on Thank U,
 Next , [ 328 ] with lyrics about breakups,
 empowerment, and self-love. [ 327 ] Her sixth album, Positions , further emphasized the R&B and trap-pop sound of its two
 predecessors, with lyrics discussing sex and romance. [ 329 ] [ 330 ] Grande grew up listening mainly to urban pop and 1990s music . [ 331 ] She credited Gloria Estefan with
 inspiring her to pursue a music career after Estefan saw and complimented Grande's
 performance on a cruise ship when she was eight years old. [ 332 ] Mariah Carey and Whitney Houston are her primary vocal influences: "I
 love Mariah Carey. She is literally my favorite human being on the planet. And of
 course Whitney [Houston] as well. As far as vocal influences go, Whitney and Mariah
 pretty much cover it." [ 333 ] Grande was also influenced
 vocally by Destiny's
 Child , Celine Dion , Christina
 Aguilera , and Madonna . [ 334 ] [ 335 ] She reflected on her
 childhood by posting videos of herself singing songs from Dion's 1997 album Let's
 Talk About Love on her social media. [ 336 ] Grande credits Madonna with
 "pav[ing] the way for me and also every other female artist" and admitted to being
 "obsessed with her entire discography ". [ 337 ] [ 338 ] Musically, Grande admires India
 Arie because her "music makes me feel like everything is going to be okay",
 loves Brandy Norwood 's
 songs because "her riffs are incredibly on
 point", and praised Imogen
 Heap 's "intricate" song structure. [ 327 ] Heap in particular Grande
 has said is her favorite musician, songwriter, and producer of all time. [ 339 ] [ 340 ] Grande also named Judy Garland as a childhood
 influence, admiring her ability to tell "a story when she sings". [ 327 ] Ahead of the release of her
 debut album, Grande says its sound was inspired by Heap, Carey, Fergie , and
 Houston. [ 341 ] Music producer and
 collaborator Savan Kotecha stated that he and Grande were influenced by Lauryn Hill when creating her fourth album Sweetener and its lead single " No Tears Left to Cry ". [ 342 ] Kotecha told Variety ,
 "we were listening to Lauryn Hill about chord changes and why we stick to four
 chords all the time". [ 343 ] Grande expressed admiration for rappers' unconventional music release strategy. She
 told Billboard , "My dream has always been to
 be—obviously not a rapper, but, like, to put out music in the way that a rapper
 does. I feel like there are certain standards that pop women are held to that men
 aren't ... It's just like, 'Bruh, I just want to ... drop [music] the way these boys
 do." [ 344 ] It inspired her to release
 "Thank U, Next" without any prior announcement, which The
 Ringer called "more of a Drake move than an Ariana Grande move". [ 345 ] Grande has been described as a soprano , [ 346 ] [ 347 ] [ 348 ] possessing a four-octave vocal range [ 6 ] [ 349 ] and a whistle register . [ 350 ] With the release of Yours
 Truly , critics compared Grande's wide vocal range and music to those of
 Mariah Carey. [ 351 ] [ 352 ] Julianne Escobedo Shepherd
 of Billboard wrote that both Carey and Grande have "the talent to let their
 vocals do the talking ... that's not where the similarities end. ... Grande is
 subverting it with cute, comfortable, and on-trend dresses with a feminine
 slant." [ 353 ] Mark Savage of BBC News named Grande "one of pop's most intriguing and gifted
 singers" and complimented her "unrivalled vocal control". [ 6 ] In The New York
 Times , Jon Pareles noted
 that Grande's voice "can be silky, breathy or cutting, swooping through long
 melismas or jabbing out short R&B phrases; it's always supple and airborne,
 never forced." [ 354 ] Composer and playwright Jason Robert
 Brown wrote in a 2016 Time magazine article, "[N]o matter how much
 you are underestimated ... you are going to open your mouth and that unbelievable
 sound is going to come out. That [...] instrument [...] allows you to shut down
 every objection and every obstacle." [ 355 ] Grande's enunciation has drawn some criticism, [ 356 ] particularly on her earlier
 recordings. [ 357 ] [ 358 ] [ 359 ] Grande herself has
 acknowledged this on multiple occasions, admitting in 2015 that pronunciation was
 something she hoped to improve. [ 360 ] However, several critics
 noted a marked improvement on Eternal Sunshine , [ 359 ] [ 361 ] with some attributing the
 clearer diction to her extensive vocal training for Wicked . [ 362 ] [ 363 ] Grande cited Audrey Hepburn as a major style influence in her early career; however, she later found emulating
 Hepburn's style "a little boring". [ 364 ] She also drew inspiration
 from actresses of the 1950s and 1960s, such as Ann-Margret , Nancy Sinatra , and Marilyn Monroe . [ 364 ] Grande's modest look early
 in her career was described as "age appropriate" in comparison to contemporary
 artists who grew up in the public eye. [ 353 ] Jim Farber of New York's New York Daily
 News wrote in 2014 that Grande received less attention "for how
 little she wears or how graphically she moves than for how she sings." [ 365 ] That year, she abandoned her
 earlier style in favor of short skirts and crop tops with knee-high boots in live
 performances and red carpet events. [ 366 ] She also began regularly
 wearing cat and bunny ears and, subsequently, oversized jackets and hoodies through
 the late 2010s—the latter articles became largely associated with her persona. [ 367 ] [ 368 ] Grande later stated that
 owing to her mental health struggles at the time, she regularly wore variations of
 the oversized sweatshirt-boots outfit as she preferred to "hide away in something
 really cozy" and "did not have the mental energy to consider clothing". [ 369 ] Grande's style is often
 imitated by social media influencers and celebrities. [ 370 ] [ 371 ] After years of dyeing her
 hair red for her role as Cat Valentine on Nickelodeon, Grande wore extensions as her
 hair recovered from damage. [ 372 ] Anne T. Donahue of MTV News noted that her "iconic" high
 ponytail has received more attention than her fashion choices. [ 373 ] Although Grande drew criticism for alleged impolite interactions with reporters and
 fans in 2014, [ 374 ] she dismissed the reports as
 "weird, inaccurate depictions". [ 3 ] Rolling Stone wrote:
 "Some may cry 'diva', but it's also Grande just taking a stand to not allow others
 to control her image." [ 375 ] In July 2015, Grande sparked
 controversy after being seen on surveillance video in a doughnut shop licking
 doughnuts that were on display and saying "I hate Americans. I hate America. This is
 disgusting", referring to a tray of doughnuts. [ 376 ] She subsequently apologized,
 saying that she is "extremely proud to be an American" and that her comments rather
 referred to obesity in the United States . [ 377 ] She later released a video
 apology for "behaving poorly". [ 378 ] The incident was parodied by The
 Muppets . [ 379 ] Grande herself poked fun at
 the incident while hosting Saturday Night Live in 2016, saying, "A lot of kid
 stars end up doing drugs, or in jail, or pregnant, or get caught licking a doughnut
 they didn't pay for." [ 6 ] [ 380 ] In 2020, she admitted to
 refraining from interviews for a while out of fear of being labeled a "diva" and
 that her words would be misconstrued. [ 381 ] With a large following on social media, Grande is one of the most influential
 celebrities on the internet. [ 382 ] [ 383 ] As of March 2025 [update] ,
 her YouTube channel has over 57 million subscribers, making her the third-most-subscribed female
 solo act and fourth-most-subscribed woman on the platform. [ 384 ] Her channel has received
 over 31 billion views; eight of Grande's music videos have over one billion views on
 YouTube, [ 385 ] [ 386 ] of which two have surpassed
 two billion views, [ 387 ] with her highest-viewed
 video having over 2.4 billion views. [ 388 ] Her Spotify profile has over
 110 million followers, [ 389 ] making her the seventh-most-followed artist
 and third-most-followed woman . [ 390 ] She is the sixth-most-followed individual
 on Instagram , [ 391 ] and was the first woman to
 surpass 150 million and 200 million followers on the platform. [ 392 ] [ 393 ] She was the most-followed
 woman on the platform from February 2019 to January 2022. [ 394 ] [ 395 ] In December 2021, Grande
 deleted her Twitter account, which was one of the most-followed accounts on the
 platform. [ 396 ] [ 397 ] She explained that she
 "always wanted to say things to [her] fans that were meant for just [her] fans [...]
 sometimes it would travel in a way that it wasn't intended to [...] where people who
 don't speak our language would kind of become involved in a weird, strange way. I
 think I was just so sensitive [and] it started taking toll on my relationship to
 work. I wanted to prioritize being an artist and having a healthy relationship to my
 fans and to art". [ 398 ] Often regarded as a pop icon and triple threat entertainer, [ 399 ] [ 400 ] wax figures of Grande are found at Madame Tussauds museums
 in various cities around the world, including New York City , [ 401 ] Orlando, Florida , [ 402 ] Amsterdam , [ 403 ] Bangkok , [ 404 ] Sydney , [ 405 ] Berlin , [ 406 ] London , [ 407 ] Vienna , [ 408 ] Hollywood , [ 409 ] Hong Kong , [ 410 ] and Blackpool . [ 411 ] In 2016 and 2019, Grande was named one of Time ' s 100 most influential people in the world . [ 355 ] [ 412 ] In 2017, Celia Almeida of
 the Miami New
 Times wrote that of all the biggest pop stars of the past 20 years,
 Grande made the most convincing transition "from ingénue to an independent female
 artist". [ 413 ] Bloomberg News named her
 the "first pop diva of the streaming generation" in 2020. [ 414 ] Regarded as a pop icon , Grande was nicknamed " Princess of Pop " by Guinness
 World Records . [ 415 ] Due to her 2014 song "Santa
 Tell Me" becoming a 21st-century Christmas standard and having a lasting impact,
 Grande was dubbed the "Princess of Christmas". [ 416 ] [ 417 ] Grande was also included in Pitchfork 's list of "The 200 Most
 Important Artists of Pitchfork's First 25 Years" for "emerging with music that
 pushed her artistry further as it asserted a magical trifecta of hope, joy, and a
 powerhouse voice". [ 418 ] Her song "Thank U, Next" was
 ranked number 137 in Rolling Stone 's 2021 revision of their 500 Greatest Songs of All Time , [ 419 ] while its parent album was
 ranked number 61 in their "250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century". [ 420 ] In 2023, the magazine ranked
 Grande among the 200 Greatest Singers of All Time, at number 43. [ 421 ] The
 Hollywood Reporter named her as one of its "Platinum Power Players"
 in music in 2024. [ 422 ] In May that year, Katy Perry declared Grande to be
 "the best singer of our generation". [ 423 ] Billboard ranked
 Grande at number nine on its 2024 " Greatest Pop
 Stars of the 21st Century " list, [ 424 ] and at number eight on its
 2025 list of the "Top 100 Women Artists of the 21st Century". [ 425 ] The magazine ranked her
 album Thank U, Next at number 144 out of 200 on its "Top 200 Billboard 200 Albums of the 21st Century" in 2025. [ 426 ] Recording artists who have cited Grande as an influence or inspiration include Billie Eilish , [ 427 ] Breanna Yde , [ 428 ] Bryson Tiller , [ 429 ] Chappell Roan , [ 430 ] Charlie Puth , [ 431 ] Giselle of Aespa , [ 432 ] Grace VanderWaal , [ 433 ] Jungkook of BTS , [ 434 ] Lana Del Rey , [ 435 ] Madison Beer , [ 371 ] Maggie Lindemann , [ 436 ] Meghan Trainor , [ 437 ] Melanie Martinez , [ 438 ] Michelle Zauner of Japanese
 Breakfast , [ 439 ] Sufjan Stevens , [ 440 ] Tate McRae , [ 441 ] Troye Sivan , [ 442 ] and Zara Larsson . [ 443 ] Grande has sold over 90 million records worldwide, [ 444 ] making her one of the best-selling music artists of all
 time. All of Grande's studio albums have been certified platinum or higher by the Recording Industry Association
 of America (RIAA) and have spent at least one year charting on the Billboard 200 chart.
 Her highest-certified album by the RIAA is My Everything , at
 quadruple platinum, [ 445 ] whilst her longest-charting
 album, Thank U, Next , has spent 185 non-consecutive weeks on the chart. [ 446 ] Grande has accumulated 15
 million albums and 124 million digital singles units as a lead artist in the United
 States, [ 447 ] making her the
 13th-highest-certified artist and fourth-highest-certified female artist on RIAA's Top Artists
 (Digital Singles) ranking. [ 448 ] With 139 million units
 combined (songs and albums), she is the 21st-highest-certified artist, overall, and
 sixth-highest among women. [ 449 ] In the US, Grande has moved
 22.4 million album units, and garnered over 23.6 billion streams across lead artist
 credits, as of 2023, according to Luminate . [ 450 ] [ 451 ] Two of her songs have been
 certified diamond by the RIAA: "Bang Bang" (with Jessie J and Nicki Minaj ) and "7 Rings". [ 452 ] Having surpassed 98 billion streams globally as of 2021, Grande is one of the
 most-streamed artists of all time and was the first female artist to surpass 90
 billion streams. [ 286 ] [ 453 ] She was the most-streamed
 female artist of the 2010s decade on Spotify , being the only woman in the overall top five. [ 143 ] She was also the
 most-streamed female act of the 2010s decade on Apple Music , and was the first female act to reach 3
 billion total streams on the platform. [ 454 ] In the US, Grande was the
 most-streamed female artist and fourth-most-streamed artist overall of the 2010s
 decade, across audio and video streams, being the only woman and non-rapper in the
 top five. [ 455 ] She became the most-streamed
 female artist of all time on Spotify in 2020, surpassing Rihanna , and held the record for over two years. [ 456 ] As of January 2026, Grande
 is the second-most-streamed woman and the sixth-most-streamed act on Spotify, with
 over 63 billion streams across all credits (including 52 billion streams as a lead
 artist). She is the second woman in the platform's history to surpass 60 billion
 total streams. [ 457 ] Her songs and albums are some of the most-streamed of all
 time . Grande became the first woman with one and two billion streams with
 one album, [ 458 ] 3.5 billion streams on three
 separate albums, [ 459 ] and the first artist to have
 five albums with four billion streams. [ 460 ] Grande has 22 songs with
 over one billion streams on Spotify, making her the female artist with the most
 songs to have achieved the feat; [ 461 ] she was the first woman to
 have 22 songs surpass the mark. [ 462 ] [ 463 ] In 2024, Grande became the first artist to have five albums with multiple songs with
 over a billion streams on the streaming platform. [ 464 ] In December 2025, she became
 the first woman with over 126.8 million monthly listeners on the app, achieving the
 highest number of all time for a female act. [ 465 ] She has also topped
 Spotify's monthly listener ranking the most times (5) among women. [ 466 ] Grande is the seventh-most-followed artist
 and fourth-most-followed female artist on Spotify, with over 110 million
 followers; [ 390 ] she is the fourth artist in
 the streaming service's history to surpass 100 million followers. [ 467 ] Her 2014 single "Santa Tell
 Me" is the most-streamed Christmas song released in the 2010s—and
 third-most-streamed overall—on Spotify; the most successful holiday song released in
 the 21st century; and the eighth-most-popular holiday song of all time. [ 468 ] [ 469 ] Grande is the
 third-most-subscribed female soloist on YouTube, with over 57 million
 subscribers. [ 384 ] Eight of her music videos
 have surpassed over one billion views; two of them have received over two billion
 views on the app. [ 386 ] [ 387 ] Grande has won three Grammy Awards , [ 470 ] one Brit
 Award , [ 471 ] thirteen MTV Video Music Awards (the fifth-most wins
 among women), [ 472 ] [ 473 ] three MTV Europe
 Music Awards , [ 474 ] and three American Music Awards . [ 475 ] She has received 42 Billboard Music Award nominations and
 won 2 in 2019, including Top Female Artist . [ 170 ] Grande has won eleven Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards ,
 including one in 2014 for Favorite TV
 Actress for her performance on Sam & Cat , [ 476 ] and one in 2025 for Favorite Movie
 Actress for her performance in Wicked . [ 477 ] She has received three People's Choice Awards . [ 478 ] In 2014, she received the
 Breakthrough Artist of the Year Award from the Music Business Association [ 55 ] and Best Newcomer at the Bambi
 Awards . [ 479 ] She has won six iHeartRadio Music Awards [ 480 ] and twelve Teen Choice
 Awards . [ 481 ] She was named Billboard Women in Music's Rising Star in 2014 [ 482 ] and Woman of
 the Year in 2018, [ 483 ] the greatest pop star of
 2019, with honorable mentions in 2014 and 2018; and the most successful female
 artist to debut in the 2010s by Billboard . [ 184 ] [ 484 ] Grande was named one of the
 ten best-selling global recording artists of
 2018, 2019, and 2020 by the International
 Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), being the highest-ranked
 woman of 2018 (number eight). [ 485 ] [ 486 ] [ 487 ] The IFPI ranked her as 2024
 and 2025's eleventh-best-selling recording artist globally. [ 273 ] [ 488 ] For acting, Grande has been
 nominated for an Academy Award , two Golden Globe Awards , two Critics' Choice awards, and a BAFTA Award , Screen Actors Guild Award , and Satellite
 Award each. [ 296 ] Nine singles by Grande have topped the Billboard Hot 100 , her most recent being " We Can't Be Friends (Wait
 for Your Love) ". [ 255 ] Grande has a total of
 twenty-three top-ten songs on the chart, which includes sixteen top-ten debuts thus
 far, beginning with her first single " The Way "; the lead single from each of
 her first seven studio albums have debuted in the top ten, making her the only
 artist to achieve this. [ 489 ] In 2020, she became the
 first act to have her first five number-one singles, " Thank U,
 Next ", " 7 Rings ", " Stuck With
 U ", " Rain on Me ", and " Positions " debut at
 number one; that year, Grande also broke the record for the most number one debuts
 and became the first female artist topping Global 200, Global 200 Excl. US and Hot 100
 simultaneously . [ 200 ] Grande would also become the
 first artist to have three singles debut at number one on a single calendar
 year. [ 209 ] She later broke the record
 for most simultaneously charting songs on the top 40 of the Hot 100 for a female
 artist with the release of her fifth studio album, Thank U, Next , when eleven of the twelve
 tracks charted within the region (later surpassed by Billie Eilish ). [ 162 ] The three singles from Thank U, Next , "7 Rings", " Break Up with Your
 Girlfriend, I'm Bored ", and "Thank U, Next" charted at numbers one, two, and
 three respectively on the week of February 23, 2019, making Grande the first solo
 artist to occupy the top three spots of the Billboard Hot 100 and the first
 artist to do so since the Beatles in 1964. [ 160 ] With her album Thank U,
 Next , Grande set the record for the largest streaming week for a pop album
 and for a female artist at the time, with 307 million on-demand audio streams. [ 156 ] With "Die for You" with the Weeknd reaching number one,
 she surpassed Paul McCartney as the artist with the most number-one duets in Hot 100
 history, with four songs. In December 2025, Grande became the third woman in history
 to chart eight albums simultaneously on the Billboard 200, joining Taylor Swift and Whitney Houston . [ 490 ] As of March 2026 [update] ,
 Grande has 98 chart entries—the fourth-most among women—on the Hot 100. [ 491 ] She is the female artist
 with the second-most number-one debuts on the Hot 100 (7). [ 492 ] On the Billboard Pop Airplay chart, Grande has
 10 number-ones and 23 top-ten songs. [ 493 ] She was also named the Billboard year-end Top Female Artist of 2017 and 2019 and was ranked sixth
 among women (twelfth overall) on the magazine's decade-end Top Artists Chart for the
 2010s, the highest for any female act to have debuted that decade. [ 494 ] [ 495 ] [ 496 ] The magazine also ranked her
 as the sixth-greatest pop star of 2024, [ 497 ] [ 498 ] 78th on the "Greatest of All
 Time Hot 100 Artists" chart, [ 499 ] [ 500 ] and 19th on their "Top
 Artists of the 21st Century" list. [ 501 ] As of 2025, Grande has broken 40 Guinness World Records . [ 502 ] [ 503 ] These records included the
 most songs to debut at number one on the Billboard Hot 100, most followers on
 Spotify (female), most monthly listeners on Spotify (female), most-streamed act on
 Spotify (female), most streamed track in one week by a female artist on the
 Billboard charts, fastest hat-trick of UK No. 1 singles by a female artist, first
 female artist to replace herself at No. 1 on UK singles chart, first solo artist to
 replace themselves at No. 1 on UK singles chart for two consecutive weeks, most
 subscribers for a musician on YouTube (female), most streamed album by a female
 artist in one week (UK), among others. Eleven records were achieved from the success
 of her album Thank U, Next which was featured in the 2020 edition.

sections.heading: Philanthropy and activism
sections.text:
At age ten, Grande co-founded the South Florida youth singing group Kids Who Care,
 which performed at charitable fund-raisers and raised over $500,000 in 2007
 alone. [ 504 ] In 2009, as a member of the
 charitable organization Broadway in South Africa, she and her brother Frankie
 performed and taught music and dance to children in Gugulethu , South Africa. [ 505 ] [ 506 ] She was featured with Bridgit
 Mendler and Kat Graham in Seventeen magazine in a 2013
 public campaign to end online bullying called "Delete Digital Drama". [ 507 ] After watching the film Blackfish that
 year, she urged fans to stop supporting SeaWorld . [ 4 ] In September 2014, Grande
 participated at the charitable Stand Up to Cancer television program, performing
 her song "My Everything" in memory of her grandfather, who had died of cancer that
 July. [ 508 ] Grande has adopted several
 rescue dogs as pets and has promoted pet adoption at her concerts. [ 509 ] In 2016, she launched a line
 of lip shades, "Ariana Grande's MAC Viva Glam", with MAC Cosmetics, the profits of
 which benefited people affected by HIV and AIDS. [ 510 ] [ 511 ] That same year, Grande and Andrea Martin participated
 in the Children of Armenia Fund (COAF) gala
 concert, a benefit for raising funds for impoverished children in Armenia , by encouraging people to buy
 tickets in support. [ 512 ] [ 513 ] In 2015, Grande and Miley Cyrus performed a cover of Crowded
 House 's " Don't Dream It's Over " as part of
 Cyrus's " Backyard
 Sessions " to benefit her Happy Hippie Foundation , which helps
 homeless and LGBTQ youths. [ 514 ] Later that year, Grande
 headlined the Dance On the Pier event, part of the LGBT Pride Week in New York
 City. [ 515 ] As a feminist, Grande wrote
 a well-received, "empowering" essay on Twitter decrying the double standard and
 misogyny in the focus of the press on female musicians' relationships and sex lives
 instead of "their value as an individual". [ 516 ] [ 517 ] She said that she has "more
 to talk about" concerning her music and accomplishments rather than her romantic
 relationships. [ 518 ] [ 519 ] That year, Grande joined Madonna to raise funds for orphaned
 children in Malawi ; [ 520 ] she and Victoria Monét recorded "Better Days" in support of the Black Lives Matter movement. [ 521 ] To aid the victims of the Manchester Arena bombing in 2017, Grande
 organized the One
 Love Manchester concert and re-released "One Last Time" and her live
 performance of " Over the
 Rainbow " at the event as charity singles. [ 522 ] [ 523 ] The total amount raised was
 reportedly $23 million (more than £17 million), [ 372 ] [ 113 ] and she received praise for
 her "grace and strength" in leading the benefit concert. [ 524 ] [ 522 ] Madeline Roth of MTV wrote
 that the performance "bolstered courage among an audience that desperately needed
 it. ... Returning to the stage was a true act of bravery and resilience". [ 525 ] In 2017, New
 York magazine's Vulture section ranked the event as the No. 1
 concert of the year, [ 526 ] and Billboard 's Mitchell Harrison
 called Grande a "gay icon" for her LGBTQ-friendly lyrics and performances and
 "support for the LGBTQ community". [ 527 ] In September 2017, Grande performed in A Concert for Charlottesville which benefitted the victims of the August 2017 white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia . [ 528 ] In March 2018, she
 participated in March for Our Lives to support gun control
 reform. [ 529 ] Grande donated the proceeds
 from the first show in Atlanta on her Sweetener World Tour to Planned Parenthood in a
 response to the passage of a number of anti-abortion laws in several states
 including Georgia . [ 530 ] [ 531 ] During the COVID-19 pandemic ,
 Grande donated between $500 and $1,000 each to a number of fans as financial
 support. [ 532 ] Grande also supported a COVID-19 fund named Project
 100 , which aimed to provide $1,000 digital payments to 100,000 families who
 have been greatly impacted by the pandemic. [ 533 ] In May 2020, Grande announced that all net proceeds from her collaboration with
 singer Justin Bieber , "Stuck
 With U", would be donated to the First Responders Children's Foundation to fund
 grants and scholarships for children of frontline workers who are working during the global pandemic . [ 197 ] That month, Grande joined a
 Los Angeles protest against the murder of George Floyd , demanding justice and
 asking fans to sign petitions condemning the act of police brutality. She
 highlighted white privilege and called for more activism outside social media. [ 534 ] [ 535 ] In 2022, Grande surprised
 children, who were spending the Christmas holiday period at hospitals in Manchester,
 with gifts from wish lists at the Royal Manchester Children's
 Hospital , among others. Manchester Foundation Trust Charity revealed that
 Grande had gifted nearly 1,000 presents to patients across the hospital network's
 children's wards and newborn intensive care units in 2021. [ 536 ] In June 2021, Grande and other celebrities signed an open letter to Congress
 requesting passage of the Equality Act , highlighting that the Act
 would protect "marginalized communities". [ 537 ] In the same month, Grande
 partnered with the online portal BetterHelp , and gave away $2 million worth of therapy to
 fans. [ 538 ] [ 539 ] On International Transgender
 Day of Visibility in 2022, she launched the Protect & Defend Trans Youth
 Fund to benefit transgender youth , pledging to match every
 donation up until $1.5 million. [ 540 ] In May 2022, Grande was
 among 160 artists and influencers, who signed a 'Bans Off Our
 Bodies' full-page advertisement in The New York Times , in support of
 abortion rights in the US. [ 541 ] Grande was also one of 175
 entertainers to sign an open letter to oppose books bans in US schools in 2023. [ 542 ] In June 2022, Grande
 endorsed Karen Bass for 2022 Los
 Angeles mayoral election. [ 543 ] In 2023, Grande signed an open letter from Artists4Ceasefire to president Joe Biden during the Gaza war . [ 544 ] [ 545 ] In May 2024, after Israel launched an
 airstrike on Rafah , Grande shared a fundraiser aimed at providing
 humanitarian aid for Palestinians in Gaza. [ 546 ] Following Biden's withdrawal from the 2024 US presidential election , Grande
 showed support for vice president Kamala Harris 's campaign . [ 547 ] In January 2025, she
 reposted messaging from the nonprofit organization Advocates for Trans Equality , via her
 social media, in response to US President Donald Trump's order to withdraw federal
 recognition for transgender people. [ 548 ] The following month, Grande
 advocated for therapy for young entertainers in both the acting and music fields,
 saying that weekly appointments should be built into their contracts. [ 549 ] That June, she endorsed Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez 's recommendation
 to impeach Trump for a "disastrous decision to bomb Iran without
 authorization". [ 550 ]

sections.heading: Products and endorsements
sections.text:
In November 2015, she released a limited edition handbag in collaboration with Coach . [ 551 ] In January 2016, she
 launched a makeup collection with MAC Cosmetics , donating 100% of proceeds to the MAC AIDS
 Fund . [ 552 ] In February 2016, Grande
 launched a fashion line with Lipsy London. [ 553 ] Later that year, she teamed
 up with Brookstone , using the
 concept art of artist Wenqing Yan, to design cat ear headphones. [ 554 ] In 2017, Grande collaborated
 with Square Enix to create a
 character based on herself for the mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius .
 Grande was a limited-time unlockable character as part of the Dangerous Woman
 Tour event, which also included an orchestral remix of Grande's song "Touch
 It"; the character, Dangerous Ariana, is a magical support character who uses
 music-based attacks. [ 555 ] [ 556 ] In September 2017, she
 became a brand ambassador for Reebok . [ 557 ] In August 2018, she partnered with American Express for The Sweetener
 Sessions , a partnership which continued through the Sweetener World
 Tour in 2019, alongside T-Mobile . In March 2019, she partnered with Starbucks for the launch of the
 Cloud Macchiato beverage. [ 558 ] In May 2019, Grande was
 announced as the face of Givenchy 's
 fall-winter campaign. [ 559 ] The campaign began in July
 and generated $25.13 million in media impact value . [ 560 ] In July 2024, she became the
 brand ambassador of Swarovski ;
 Grande's first appearance as the face was in the house's holiday campaign in October
 2024. [ 561 ] [ 562 ] Grande collaborated with the
 company's global creative director Giovanna Battaglia Engelbert on two
 capsule collections, released in January 2025 and March 2026. [ 563 ] [ 564 ] Beats , Samsung , Fiat , Reebok, and Guess products have been featured in
 Grande's music videos. [ 565 ] She has appeared in
 commercials for Macy's , T-Mobile,
 and Apple , as well as for her own
 fragrances. [ 566 ] Since 2019, Grande has been
 among the ten highest-paid individuals on Instagram. As of 2025, Grande earns $2
 million per sponsored Instagram post. [ 567 ] [ 568 ] Grande has released eighteen fragrances with Luxe Brands. She launched her debut
 fragrance, Ari by Ariana Grande, in 2015. In the wake of its success, she launched
 her third fragrance, Sweet Like Candy, in 2016. [ 569 ] Her fifth fragrance,
 Moonlight, was released in 2017, followed by Cloud (2018), Thank U, Next (2019),
 R.E.M. (2020), and God Is a Woman (2021), which was later expanded to an Ulta -exclusive body care line
 in 2022. [ 570 ] She then released the duo
 fragrance collection Mod Vanilla and Mod Blush (2022). [ 571 ] It was followed by the
 collection Lovenotes (2024), which consisted of four region-exclusive
 fragrances. [ 572 ] The next fragrance was Cherry Blossom (2025), released as a R.E.M. Beauty product via
 Ulta. [ 573 ] The range also includes the
 limited editions Frankie (2016), Sweet Like Candy Limited Edition (2017), Thank U,
 Next 2.0, Cloud Intense (both 2021), and Cloud Pink (2023). The fragrances won the FiFi Award multiple times, most recently with R.E.M. in 2021. In 2022, it was reported that
 Cloud was the best-selling fragrance at Ulta, selling one bottle every eleven
 seconds. [ 574 ] As of 2024, the scents are
 developed and manufactured in collaboration with Robertet Group and International Flavors &
 Fragrances . [ 575 ] Grande's fragrance line is
 the most-searched celebrity offering, with over 4.4 million searches across Google
 and social media platforms per year, as of 2023. [ 576 ] Since its launch in 2015,
 the franchise has made over $1 billion in retail sales globally. [ 577 ] In November 2021, Grande launched her makeup line R.E.M. Beauty, which is distributed
 at Ulta Beauty as of March 2022. [ 578 ] [ 579 ] The original line featured
 12 core products for lips and eyes, and the range has since been expanded with
 additional skincare and makeup products. [ 578 ] [ 580 ] Forbes reported in 2022 that R.E.M. Beauty was one of
 the brands boosting Ulta's driving gross margin due to strong consumer demand. [ 581 ] In May, the line won "Best
 New Brand" at the Allure Best of Beauty Awards . [ 582 ] In February 2023, the brand
 was launched in 81 Sephora stores and 13
 online sites, including across Europe. [ 583 ] Grande has said she struggled with hypoglycemia , which she attributed to poor dietary
 habits. [ 584 ] She has been following a vegan diet since
 2013, [ 585 ] though fans questioned in
 2019 whether she still was, after working with Starbucks to create a special edition of one of her
 favorite drinks which was revealed to contain eggs. Her nutritionist, Harley
 Pasternak, told the magazine Glamour that Grande is still following the
 diet, but that he has gotten her to "feel OK about indulging and celebrating
 sometimes". [ 586 ] Grande developed post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
 and anxiety after the Manchester
 Arena bombing ; she nearly pulled out of her performance in the 2018
 broadcast A Very Wicked Halloween due to
 anxiety. [ 587 ] Grande has also said she has
 been in therapy for over a decade, having first seen a mental health professional
 shortly after her parents' divorce. [ 588 ] Grande was raised Catholic , but left the church during the pontificate of Benedict
 XVI (circa 2013), [ 589 ] opposing its stance on homosexuality [ 4 ] and stating that her
 half-brother Frankie is gay. [ 590 ] Grande said that she and
 Frankie later visited a Kabbalah Centre and that they both "really had a
 connection with it". [ 3 ] [ 590 ] Several of her songs, such
 as "Break Your Heart Right Back", are supportive of LGBT rights . [ 591 ] She has also been labeled
 "an advocate for a sex-positive attitude". [ 592 ] In November 2019, Grande endorsed Bernie Sanders 's second presidential
 bid . [ 593 ] She endorsed Joe Biden for the 2020 presidential
 election , [ 594 ] and Kamala Harris for the 2024 presidential
 election . [ 595 ] In June 2025, amid ICE enforcement operations in Los
 Angeles , Grande wrote on Instagram that she was "deeply upset about these
 violent deportations" and that "LA simply wouldn't exist without immigrants",
 sharing ACLU resources on immigrant
 rights. [ 596 ] In January 2026, Grande
 promoted a nationwide protest against ICE on her Instagram Story, urging followers
 to participate in the "ICE Out Nationwide Shutdown" on January 30. [ 597 ] At the 83rd Golden Globe Awards on January 11,
 2026, Grande wore an "ICE Out" pin on her Vivienne Westwood dress, part of a coordinated
 campaign in response to the fatal shooting of Renee
 Good by an ICE agent in Minneapolis . [ 598 ] [ 599 ] Grande's personal relationships have been widely scrutinized by the public. [ 600 ] Some of her former lovers
 were mentioned by name in the song " Thank U, Next ". [ 601 ] She dated her 13 co-star Graham
 Phillips for three years. [ 602 ] [ 603 ] [ 604 ] From August 2012 to August
 2014, Grande was in an on-again, off-again relationship with Australian YouTuber Jai Brooks . [ 605 ] She briefly dated English
 singer Nathan Sykes during
 their separation, and then dated rapper Big Sean for eight months. [ 606 ] Grande was in a year-long
 relationship with Ricky Alvarez, who was one of her backup dancers on the Honeymoon
 Tour . [ 607 ] [ 608 ] After recording " The Way " in 2012, Grande began dating
 rapper Mac Miller in 2016. [ 609 ] [ 610 ] She was prominently featured
 on his fourth album The Divine Feminine (2016), including on
 its third single " My
 Favorite Part ". [ 611 ] [ 612 ] By May 2018, their
 relationship had ended and Grande entered a whirlwind romance with comedian Pete Davidson . [ 613 ] They got engaged in June,
 after a few weeks of dating, while a song titled after and inspired by Davidson was
 featured on Sweetener . [ 614 ] That September, Miller died from an accidental drug
 overdose ; Grande expressed grief over his death on social media and called
 him her "dearest friend". [ 615 ] She and Davidson called off
 their engagement and ended their relationship the following month. [ 616 ] Grande began dating real estate agent Dalton Gomez in January 2020. [ 617 ] Their relationship, while
 mostly private, was made public in May 2020, in the music video of her and Justin Bieber 's charity
 single " Stuck with U ". [ 618 ] Grande announced their
 engagement on December 20, 2020, after 11 months of dating. [ 619 ] On May 15, 2021, they
 married in a private ceremony at her home in Montecito, California. [ 620 ] Her wedding pictures became the second-most-liked Instagram
 post and most-liked Instagram post featuring pictures of people at the time,
 with over 25 million likes. [ 621 ] [ 622 ] Grande and Gomez separated
 on February 20, 2023, and simultaneously filed for divorce that September due to " irreconcilable differences ". [ 623 ] They agreed on a divorce
 settlement in October, which was finalized in March 2024. [ 624 ] [ 625 ] As of July 2023, Grande is
 in a relationship with her Wicked co-star Ethan Slater . [ 626 ] Films and television Victorious (2010–2013) Sam
 & Cat (2013–2014) Hairspray Live! (2016) Don't Look Up (2021) Wicked (2024) [ note 2 ] Brighter Days
 Ahead (2025) [ note 3 ] Wicked: For Good (2025) [ note 2 ] Documentaries and concert specials One Love

 the BBC (2018) Ariana

 Grande: Excuse Me, I Love You (2020) My Everything (2014) Dangerous

chunks.heading: Introduction
chunks.text: Ariana Grande-Butera ( / ˌ ɑːr i ˈ ɑː n ə ˈ ɡ r ɑː n d eɪ b j ʊ ˈ t ɛ ə r ə / ⓘ AR -ee- AH -nə GRAHN -day byuu- TAIR -ə ; [ note 1 ] born June 26, 1993) is an American singer, songwriter, and actress. Known for her four-octave vocal range , which extends into the whistle register , she is regarded as an influential figure in popular music . Publications such as Rolling Stone and Billboard have deemed Grande one of the greatest artists in history, while Time included her on its list of the world's 100 most influential people in 2016 and 2019. Grande's career began as a teenager in the Broadway musical 13 (2008) before she gained prominence as Cat Valentine in the Nickelodeon television series Victorious (2010–2013) and its spin-off Sam & Cat (2013–2014). After signing with Republic Records , she released her debut studio album, Yours Truly (2013), a retro -inspired pop and R&B record that debuted atop the Billboard 200 . She incorporated elements of

chunks.text: Republic Records , she released her debut studio album, Yours Truly (2013), a retro -inspired pop and R&B record that debuted atop the Billboard 200 . She incorporated elements of electronic on her next two albums, My Everything (2014) and Dangerous Woman (2016), which both achieved international success, spawning the singles " Problem ", " Break Free ", " Bang Bang ", " One Last Time ", " Into You ", and " Side to Side ". Personal struggles influenced Grande's albums Sweetener (2018) and Thank U, Next (2019), both of which delved into trap . The latter garnered the US Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles " Thank U, Next " and " 7 Rings ". With the title track of her R&B-infused album Positions (2020), as well as the collaborations " Stuck with U " and " Rain on Me ", she achieved the most number-one debuts in the US. She returned to acting with the political satire Don't Look Up (2021) and portrayed Glinda in the fantasy musical film Wicked (2024), which earned her an Academy Award nomination, as well as its sequel Wicked: For Good (2025). Grande is one of the best-selling music artists of all time , with estimated sales of over 90 million records. The highest-paid female musician in 2020, her accolades include three Grammy Awards , a Brit Award , two Billboard Music Awards , three American Music Awards , forty Guinness World Records , and thirteen MTV Video Music Awards . Six of Grande's albums have reached number one on the Billboard 200, while nine of her songs have topped the Billboard Hot 100. Outside of music and acting, she has worked with many charitable organizations and advocates for animal rights , mental health , and gender , racial , and LGBT equality . Her business ventures include the cosmetics brand R.E.M. Beauty and a fragrance line that has earned over $1 billion in global retail sales. She has a large social media following, being the sixth-most-followed individual on Instagram . Ariana Grande-Butera was born on June 26, 1993, in Boca Raton, Florida . [ 2 ] She is the daughter of Joan Grande, the Brooklyn -born CEO of Hose-McCann Communications, a manufacturer of marine communications equipment owned by the Grande family since 1964, [ 3 ] and Edward Butera, a graphic design firm owner in Boca Raton. chunks.text: At age ten, Grande co-founded the South Florida youth singing group Kids Who Care, which performed at charitable fund-raisers and raised over $500,000 in 2007 alone. [ 507 ] After watching the film Blackfish that year, she urged fans to stop supporting SeaWorld . [ 4 ] In September 2014, Grande participated at the charitable Stand Up to Cancer television program, performing her song "My Everything" in memory of her grandfather, who had died of cancer that July.
